title: Light
body:
In the process of refreshing my student apartment,
I thought it would be fitting to add a bit of "nature" to the space
by buying a plant.

I walk into the first flower shop I come across:

* Hello, I would like a small pot with an indoor plant for decoration.
Some time passed while the florist showed me all my options,
explaining to me in meticulous detail the needs of every single plant.

-This one here looks beautiful. I think I'll take this one.
-Great, just to let you know, you'll need to keep this specific one in a bright spot in the house, otherwise it will wither. It blooms winter and summer, but it has this particular requirement.

And yes, that was the exact moment I realized I was going to buy something that has life.
-But where I want to put it, there isn't much light.
-What can I say, do you want to go with a cactus instead? Or do you want to risk it?

I took the risk. And you know why? Our soul, many times, asks for nothing more than Light. Otherwise, it will wither.
We, our daily routine, society, our obligations,
insist on placing it in dark places for the sake of appearances,
indifferent to its living, breathing side.
So I decided not to go with a cactus;
not to choose the easy way out.

Because I decided to care for my Soul
like the plant:
to keep it permanently exposed to the Light.

y.f.
